title: Quiz: System Architecture - Fundamentals
prompt: Test your foundational understanding of basic computer components and CPU architecture.

questions.question: What are the three main parts that make up a Central Processing Unit (CPU)?
options: Address Bus, Data Bus, and Control Bus
Primary Memory, Secondary Memory, and the System Clock
Control Unit (CU), Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), and Registers
Keyboard, Monitor, and Hard Disk Drive
questions.explanation: The CPU consists of 3 main parts: Control Unit (CU), Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), and Registers.
questions.hint: Think about the internal components that calculate logic and control the flow of data across the chip.

questions.question: What happens to the data in Primary Memory (RAM) when the computer is powered off?
options: It is automatically moved to the hard disk drive.
It disappears because RAM is volatile.
It persists through the power cycle because RAM is non-volatile.
It is saved in the CPU registers.
questions.explanation: Primary memory is volatile, which means data disappears when powered off.
questions.hint: Consider the difference between volatile and non-volatile memory.

questions.question: In the context of computer architectures, what does the acronym RISC stand for?
questions.explanation: RISC stands for Reduced Instruction Set Computer.
questions.hint: The 'R' refers to keeping the instruction set simple so they execute in one machine cycle.

questions.question: During the first step of the fetch-execute cycle, where does the CPU fetch the next instruction from?
options: Primary memory into the Instruction Register (IR)
questions.explanation: The CPU fetches the next instruction from memory into the instruction register (IR).
questions.hint: Instructions are stored in RAM and moved to a specific CPU register to be decoded.

questions.question: How are comments appended to the end of a statement in an ARMv8 assembly program?
questions.explanation: In ARMv8, comments may be appended to the end of a statement after a // delimiter.
questions.hint: ARMv8 uses the same comment delimiter as C++ or JavaScript single-line comments.
